note: Rewritten from the original description by Silvestri (1914); the original is in Latin; the nominotypical subspecies was described on the same day as the species, and the measurements follow those of the holotype description; only the soldier and worker are described; the measurement unit mm follows the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The nominotypical subspecies is the typical form described by Silvestri 1914, with the type locality Mamou, French Guinea. Compared with var. arcuata, the soldier mandibles are straighter and less curved; compared with var. acutidens, the soldier head is larger and the mandibles shorter (1.38 mm versus 1.57 mm) and the mandibular teeth blunter.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 5 mm; head (excluding mandibles) length 2.08 mm, width 1.32 mm; mandible length 1.38 mm; antenna length 1.82 mm; hind tibia 1.17 mm. Head nearly rectangular, length about 4/5 greater than width; the prominence above the fontanelle thick and raised, reaching the level of the mandibular base; labrum large, anterior margin wide and deeply concave; mandible length nearly equal to head width, rather straight, curved only at the apex; antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 twice as long as segment 3.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Queen: body length 12 mm, abdomen width 4 mm; head length 0.94 mm, width 0.91 mm; compound eye long diameter 0.24 mm; hind tibia 1.17 mm. Body pale milky white, head chestnut, thoracic and abdominal tergites yellowish brown; fontanelle rather large, oval; compound eyes rather large and projecting; distance between the ocellus and the compound eye less than the long diameter of the ocellus. Antennae 14-segmented (the queen's antennae incomplete).
